newsitem.title: USA: Dillon Read to exit public finance business.
newsitem.headline: Dillon Read to exit public finance business.

text.p: Dillon Read & Co. said late Thursday it was exiting the municipal bond business, joining a growing list of firms leaving the field.
The firm cited tightening profit margins in municipal finance as the reason for the decision to disband its public finance department and discontinue related banking, sales and trading activities.
The firm said the move, to take effect on June 20, will affect 25 employees. Some of the professional staff will be "redeployed elsewhere within the firm," Dillon Read said in a statement.

The New York-based firm was widely hailed as the creator of so-called fare-box bonds, which spurred a major capital financing programme for the New York City Transit System. Subway fares deposited into turnstile boxes were the source of revenue to back debt payments on the bonds.
Dillon Read joins a growing list of firms that have exited the municipal bond business recently, including Alex. Brown & Sons Inc., First Boston Corp., and Lazard Freres & Co.
It ranked 33rd in underwriting last year, with 13 municipal bond issues totalling $857 million, according to Securities Data Co. It ranked 49th in 1995.
